questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I chose my study destination it was crucial that it was an English-speaking nation, so I had the opportunity to practise and improve my English skills - both in terms of language and written text. Furthermore, I chose my exchange university (Goldsmiths University of London) because they offered some modules that was not offered by my home university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had the best study abroad experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find the necessary information upon my arrival. I received all the needed information through letters from both my home university (University of Copenhagen) and Goldsmiths University.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received all the assistance that I needed when I arrived at my university. They arranged an information day, where the new exchange students where introduced to the university and the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I can recommend applying for an apartment or room through KFUK.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it may take some time to get back and forth between your home and the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got an apartment through the Danish organisation KFUK.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before my arrival I registered for my courses and got these confirmed during my introduction days together with my personal timetable.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could always reach out to my contact person at Goldsmiths if I had any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses that I wanted, so the registering process was very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it! And have patience, the process can be long, but it always works out for the best. It all becomes easier when you arrive and are able to talk to your contact person in real life and get advise and help from other students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not only did I learn a lot, I also got pushed out of my comfort zone which was challenging but needed.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All my courses was at a MA level and I think they called it level 7. I was joining classes with students who were doing a full MA at the university which created some really exiting discussions and interesting outlooks in class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses were quit similar to the style of teaching at my home university in Copenhagen - a classroom of around twenty student with a presentation made by the teacher for each class followed up by a free discussion among the students. Other courses where a bit different from the style of teaching at my home university in Copenhagen with only 6-8 student and a teacher, where the class was more student driven.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PO71046Z/PO71046C: The Politics of Human Rights (2022-23)
PO71051A: Decolonising Politics: Actions and Ideas from the Global South (2022-23)
PO71063A: Art, War, Terror (2022-23)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend future exchange students all the courses listed above, especially the course 'Decolonising Politics: Actions and Ideas from the Global South'. Here you get to read political thinkers from the global south and learn about how colonization is still affecting our minds and logics today.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Council tax if you do not get an exemption.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transport was more expensive than expected, if you have to take the overground or underground to your university. It is difficult to bike, so where ever you go you need to pay for public transport.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not join any activities or clubs during my term abroad, but there were a lot of opportunities if one likes.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of sports clubs and teams such as football or tennis, and many different creative and social activities where available for students that are into art, culture, movies and much more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not join any activities or clubs during my term abroad, but had I lived on campus I would have join the tennis club since the university had to great courts at campus.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: London is a massive city, so there is lots of great opportunities to always do something fun in the weekends or holidays. I loved to go visit new parts of the city. My favorite part of London is Hampstead (where I lived), if you need a break from the "city" life and wants to enjoy the nice little streets and the beautiful park called Hampstead Heath. Other than that it is really fun to hang out in Shoreditch or Richmond. I can also recommend taking a trip to Cotswold to see the more rural side of UK without having to travel far from London.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy. The brits are very friendly and the culture is not that different from the Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get to know your fellow classmates and maybe join some of the university clubs or activities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was not really any cultural differences that I found challenging, since it was not that different from Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness. Everywhere you go people are extremely polite. They thank the bus driver before getting off the bus, the teachers pauses to say "bless you" if you sneeze in class and if you ever need help or look lost, you can expect people to come help you. I have had the best conversations with strangers at bus stops or at the local coffee shop.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Have patience during the process
2. Dont be shy to join the class discussion 
3. Use the help your teachers offer when planing and writing your assignments

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, I think you are given all the information you need when attending Goldsmiths.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning to stand on my on and navigate in a new city and university, getting to know people from all around the world and attending courses that where super interesting.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To have faith in your own academic skills.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
